Now, fans can experience the legendary battle between Autobots and Decepticons like never before through immersive, action-packed pinball. TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye by Stern Pinball is available now in Pro, Premium, and Limited Edition (LE) models. In Stern Pinball’s TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye, players join Optimus Prime and the Autobots in their mission to stop Megatron and the Decepticons from stealing Earth’s energy, conquering Cybertron, and dominating the universe. TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye pushes mechanical innovation to new heights with a fully animatronic Megatron robot toy with an articulated fusion cannon that rotates and fires pinballs back at players. Soundwave’s cassette deck locks pinballs before launching them into high-intensity action while a custom sculpted Optimus Prime robot bash toy stands ready for battle, adding depth and spectacle to this world under glass that’s ...MORE THAN MEETS THE EYE. Players will experience the ultimate battle between Autobots and Deceptions, and can store Energon Cubes to power up, team up with the Dinobots, collect Transformers Tech Spec cards, and prepare for a climactic battle against Megatron. Players embark on missions inspired by major story arcs from the original 1984 TRANSFORMERS animated television series, and the machine integrates authentic video clips and story-driven missions that bring the brand’s legacy to life. To celebrate the 40th anniversary of THE TRANSFORMERS: THE MOVIE, the game includes a special mode featuring the iconic song “The Touch” by Stan Bush, custom call-outs from legendary voice actors including Peter Cullen (Optimus Prime) and Frank Welker (Megatron and Soundwave), and original music from Knights of Unicron. Loaded with Stern Pinball’s cutting-edge technology, TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye seamlessly blends physical and digital gameplay. Utilizing Stern’s award-winning Insider Connected platform, the machine introduces a brand-new Cyber Coin wallet system, where players can earn Cyber Coins to unlock exclusive challenge modes. The machine also features a special challenge mode, “Prime Training,” where Autobots guide players through the art of pinball mastery, and for the first time, includes a head-to-head experience that allows two players to compete simultaneously in real time. Limited to 750 games globally, the highly collectible Limited Edition model includes the updated Expression Lighting SystemTM and Speaker Expression Lighting System with TRANSFORMERS-themed game effects, a full-color mirrored backglass, full-color high-definition cabinet decals, exclusive custom pinball armor, a custom designer-autographed bottom arch, upgraded audio system, anti-reflection pinball playfield glass, shaker motor, a sequentially numbered plaque, a signed Certificate of Authenticity, and a digital Insider Connected LE owner’s badge on registration.

ads.author: David Jenkins
ads.title: Super Bug Arcade Fully Working and Restored
ads.description: Newly restored Super Bug arcade machine. Made in 1977 by Kee games. Pros Works flawlessly, game board has been serviced and recapped, sound amp has been replaced and audio has been tuned. Power supply has been tested and the big blue capacitor has been replaced. I added a fan with adjustable speed to keep the game pcb cool. Comes with all original artwork and a reproduction bezel, has the original but I’d prefer to keep it in order to make an accurate reproduction for it. Has a newer burn free color Sanyo crt monitor modified to work with the game. Comes with the original non working Black & White screen if you want it, it’s good for parts, has a blown flyback and pretty bad Super Bug screen burn. Unhacked harness. All modifications to the wiring are plug and play. No cut wires so all work can easily be reversed if you wanted to put the old screen back in. Not sure why you would though. Comes with original manuals for the game and has a printed manual for the new screen. Overall in great shape. One of the nicest looking Super Bugs you can find. Cons Original screen doesn’t work which is why it has been replaced with a working screen Original bezel is cracked and has cigarette burns hence the reproduction bezel made by Sticker Smith. Has some wear and scratch. Missing the original coin box Restoration process was recorded and is available on YouTube at “Jenxed Arcade” Currently for sale and for play at southern fried gaming expo. Feel free send me a message for more info and we can iron out the details!

ads.author: Doug Sass
ads.title: Vintage 1979 Taito Space Invaders Part II Cocktail Arcade Cabinet
ads.description: The classic 1980’s video game. This is a vintage 1979 cocktail-style arcade cabinet. It has a wood-grain laminate finish and a glass tabletop. Space Invaders II is the sequel to the original space alien vertical shooter. This is an early Taito direct import from Japan, with Japanese labels. The game was later distributed in North America by Midway as Space Invaders Deluxe. New Gameplay: * Aliens that Split: Certain crab invaders split into two separate shapeshifting units when hit. * Special UFOs: A blinking UFO appears with a random vulnerability state and point values, while later UFOs drop reinforcements. * Save Initials: High score tracking allows players to save their initials for the first time in the series. * Cutscenes: Short animations play between stages showing defeated invaders escaping or sending SOS signals. Power supply, monitor and logic boards have been recapped and tested. Original color CRT. Cabinet is clean and in good condition. No restoration work has been on the cabinet. Coin switch added for freeplay.

ads.title: Chewlix (Viewlix clone) sit down modern arcade cabinets x2
ads.description: FOR SALE: Blue and Black and red and black Chewlix (Chinese made Veiwlix sit down modern arcade cabinets). This is an earlier gen model that mirrors a Vewlix in almost every way. Asking $1650.00 each or $3000.00 for both I have removed almost all of the Chinese wiring and rewired it. There are ways to build a device that would convert all of the JAMMA signals to JVS but I am not including one in this sale. The monitors are the same one that comes with it originally. Its a flat panel 1080p with inputs for VGA and HDMI. It comes with a Sega 837-14572 JVS - 8 button JVS. The control panel is wired to light up (buttons and move panel light up) and includes all Sanwa components. Picture does not show the additional wiring for the button lights. However the buttons do light up also. The coin ash tray, tokens and magnetic coin insert are included (red set for the red cab and a blue set for the blue cab). Includes a custom CNC built sub panel that has two (2) usb plug ins, Sound control knob (uses RCA jacks) and six (6) mini buttons for various stuff. (see picture). Keys are included. It comes with a full Street Fight IV Ultra art set. Marquee is sandwiched between two pieces of plexi and it lights up also. Both cabinets are built Exactly the same just one is blue and black (Tekken artwork) and one is red and black (Street Fighter artwork). Require almost zero work. Install the JVS compatible system and off you go. They also make converters that make it to where you can install a PC or a game console. These require additional set up but are not to hard to figure out. However, it also DOES NOT come with a system inside. That would be a separate conversation as I have the following systems available/ Two (2) Heavy modified Taito Type X3 One (1) Modified Namco 246 One (1) Modified Namco 256 One (1) Full SNK Neo Geo motherboard, wiring, memory card, and sound board from a cabinet and yellow Neo Geo MVS multi cart Like I said there is NO syetm included with the cabinet sales. ads.title: Gate Of Doom 1990 Full Size Stand Up Arcade Game
ads.description: Gate of Doom, known in Japan as Dark Seal (ダークシール), is a hack 'n slash game developed by Data East and released in 1990 for arcades. Gate of Doom is a hack 'n slash game which uses a top-down, isometric perspective. Players can choose between four different characters, each with their own characteristics and abilities. The player can move and attack in eight directions, as well as unleash a powerful spell once its accumulated enough magic power. Much like in Karnov, the player can pick between available spells by tapping the joystick left and right. Levels are filled with enemies and traps, as well as treasure chests which the player can open to obtain various items and power-ups which give passive boosts to the character.

ads.author: Joshua Beecham
ads.title: Arcade Cabinet Project - Cabinet Shell and other parts - $200
ads.description: Empty arcade cabinet shell. Perfect restoration project for an arcade enthusiast, retro gamer, or father-and-son build. The cabinet was built from scratch using 3/4" MDF and includes: 32" portrait-mounted TV with Lexan bezel Marquee fluorescent light Cabinet shell The TV has older inputs including VGA and DVI, and may also have HDMI. Please note: the cabinet has been stored on a screened porch for several years and is dusty. It will need cleaning and some refurbishment before being put back into service. I originally built this for myself and planned to build another one someday, so I removed many of the reusable components when I retired it. It worked perfectly when I disassembled it all. We can some testing from my back porch if you want. Cabinet shell + TV + marquee light: $50 or make offer Optional components available separately: Mini-fridge - $35 Fits perfectly in the bottom of the cabinet. Holds roughly 18-24 cans. Speakers and Amplifier - $25 Generic car speakers and cheap amp. Nothing fancy, but they sounded great in the cabinet. Control Panel - $100 This was the most labor-intensive part of the build. Includes: 12 quality arcade buttons Dual joysticks Trackball Mini-PAC Opti USB controller The Mini-PAC Opti alone sells for around $69 new. The trackball has a cracked plastic piece that will need repair or replacement. Arcade PC - $30 Windows XP machine configured to boot directly into a MAME front end. The hardware itself isn't particularly valuable, but the software setup and configuration took significant time. You could also replace it with a Raspberry Pi running RetroPie or another arcade emulator solution. Pricing Summary Cabinet + TV + marquee light: $50/make offer Mini-fridge: $35 Speakers + amp: $25 Control panel: $100 Arcade PC: $30 Take everything for $200. or make offer The cabinet itself priced low because I need the space. The accessories are the parts I'd originally planned to keep for a future build, but my wife would be thrilled if they disappeared too. Pickup is only available between 6pm and 9pm weekdays and most anytime next weekend. No delivery. You will need your own truck or SUV. I expect this to be gone after Sunday July 26th. This is less of an arcade machine and more of a starting point if you want to *make* one. I offer no guarantees or support.
